subject: Data routing & deletion: processing locations, subprocessor handoffs, and export controls
messages:
From: Steven Brooks <steven.brooks@medsys.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@medsys.io>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Residency + deletion: where our inference data travels?

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot and need a focused Q&A for procurement/legal. High-level asks: where are inference requests and artifacts processed, which subprocessors touch the data, and what happens on account termination? Specifics we need:

- Primary processing regions for hosted API (and fallback regions if capacity spikes).
- Which cloud subprocessors perform GPU inference, caching, or log storage (please name vendors and locations).
- Is there any automatic cross-border transfer for hosted workloads? If so, under what circumstances?
- Data retention/deletion: timeline for user content, cached KV/prefix caches, logs, and embeddings after we terminate the account.
- Any guarantees or options to ensure US-only processing (contractual or Dedicated/Private options).
- Evidence we can share with our security team: SOC2, KMS/encryption at rest, and a subprocessor roster.

If you can provide a short summary and any artifacts we can hand to legal/security, that would be ideal. We may follow up with a few clarifying questions.

Best,
Steven
Director of Cloud Integrations
MedSys Health

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Residency + deletion: where our inference data travels?

Hi Steven — thanks for the clear list. Putting Connor and Marissa on this thread to pull the inventory and confirm timelines. Quick summary while we gather docs:

- Hosted API: primary execution in the configured region (US customers default to us-west-2). We have regional failover that may route to a nearby US region (e.g., us-east-1) during capacity or outage; we do not route hosted requests to EU/APAC unless the account region is set to those regions.
- Subprocessors: inference runs on cloud GPU providers (Redwood-managed pools). We maintain an internal subprocessor roster — Connor will attach the list and locations.
- Cross-border transfers: not automatic for US-region accounts; transfers to other geos occur only when routing policies require it (failover) or if customer uses a cross-region integration (we document these cases).
- Deletion: typical hosted-account retention is 30 days soft-delete for request content (searchable caches), 90 days for logs/diagnostics; embeddings/long-lived artifacts are configurable and can be set to immediate purge on contract/termination for enterprise deals.

Attaching a high-level residency map for now and will follow up with the subprocessor inventory and a short write-up for procurement.

Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Residency + deletion: where our inference data travels? — subprocessor inventory and notes

Aisha / Marissa — attaching the inventory and some notes. Key points for the reply to MedSys:

- Compute regions: Hosted US accounts use us-west-2 as primary; we have capacity pools in us-east-1 and us-west-1 as secondary. Dedicated and Private deployments run exclusively in customer VPCs/regions as configured.
- Subprocessors: primary cloud provider (named in CSV) for GPU inference; a managed cache provider for prefix/KV caching; a logging/monitoring vendor for operational telemetry (aggregated, anonymized). CSV lists vendor, service, and region (e.g., "CloudGPUCo - inference - us-west-2").
- Cross-border conditions: failover + emergency maintenance can trigger routing to secondary US pools. EU/APAC routing only for accounts expressly configured for those regions.
- Deletion specifics:
  * Request content: removed from active serving caches immediately on delete request; soft delete window 30 days to allow incident response.
  * Embeddings & model outputs: default retention 90 days for hosted accounts; can be shortened or disabled for enterprise/contracted accounts.
  * Logs/diagnostics: retained up to 90 days by default; can be extended depending on contract.
  * Physical purge: deprovisioning and crypto-shredding of associated keys occurs within 120 days for backups.
- Export control/legal note: we do not export controlled data outside of the US for accounts flagged as US-only. For customers with specific export control needs we recommend Dedicated or Private + contractual addendum.

See attached: subprocessor_inventory.csv and redwood_tos_export_controls.pdf. Happy to remove vendor names from the customer-facing doc if you want a higher-level summary.

Connor
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Steven — following up with the inventory and a concise summary you can share with security/procurement. See answers below and attached artifacts.

Short answers (customer-friendly):
- Primary processing: For hosted US accounts, inference requests are executed in our US regional pool (us-west-2). During capacity or outage events we may fail over to a secondary US pool (us-east-1). We do not route to EU/APAC for US-region accounts.
- Subprocessors: We use third-party cloud GPU providers and a managed logging/monitoring vendor. Attached CSV lists vendors and their operating regions. We can provide a redacted version for wider distribution.
- Cross-border transfers: Not automatic for US accounts. Transfers to other geos only occur for accounts configured in those regions or in rare failover/emergency cases in US-only pools.
- Retention & deletion:
  * Serving caches: cleared immediately on request; soft-delete window 30 days to allow for incident investigation.
  * Embeddings/outputs: default hosted retention 90 days; enterprise contracts can require immediate purge on termination.
  * Logs & diagnostics: default retention 90 days; can be shortened in contract.
  * Backups & key lifecycle: backups are rotated and crypto-shredded as part of deprovisioning; full physical purge timelines are up to 120 days depending on provider deletion policies.
- US-only guarantee: We can commit to US-only processing if you select Dedicated or Private deployment, or via an enterprise-hosted contract with regional pinning and routing policies (we'll add a contract clause).

Attached: residency_map.pdf (visual), subprocessor_inventory.csv (vendor+region), export_controls doc. Also linking our region docs here: https://na1.redwood.ai/docs/regions

Next steps: if you want a short vendor-facing statement (redacted vendor names) for procurement we can produce that within 48 hours. If Legal wants encryption-at-rest evidence or SOC2 artifacts, please let us know and we'll route to security for an NDA-first exchange.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
